description:
What EDBB Is

The Doctoral Program in Biotechnology and Bioengineering (EDBB) is one of EPFL's discipline-specific doctoral gateways. Instead of a single vacancy, the EDBB open positions page functions as a rolling noticeboard: labs across the Lausanne campus advertise PhD openings there, and candidates apply either through the EDBB doctoral programme or directly to an advertised project. EPFL's life sciences and bioengineering campus - home to the Institute of Bioengineering, the Brain Mind Institute and the Global Health Institute - concentrates an unusually dense mix of wet-lab biology, microengineering and instrumentation.

Funding and Employment

What a Swiss PhD contract looks like
ComponentDetails
EmploymentDoctoral candidates are employed, not granted - a Swiss employment contract with social security.
SalaryEPFL's basic doctoral-assistant salary starts from around CHF 55,225 gross per year (2026 scale) and rises with seniority.
Contract shapeTypically an initial fixed-term contract renewable through the four-year doctoral period; 100% activity rate.
TuitionDoctoral tuition at EPFL is nominal and covered within the employment framework.

Deadlines and How to Apply

Application routes
RouteDetails
EDBB admission deadlineThe doctoral programme's next application deadline is 1 November 2026; EDBB runs several admission rounds per year.
Individual positionsEach advertised project may carry its own closing date - some ads close earlier than the programme deadline, so read the individual advert.
MaterialsA single PDF with motivation letter, detailed CV and at least two references is the standard package; a few labs ask for direct email contact instead.
PlatformOnly applications through the official online platform (or the contact route named in each ad) are considered.

Who Should Apply

This page suits candidates with a master's (or equivalent) in life sciences, bioengineering, microengineering, chemistry or physics who want a PhD inside an engineering-flavoured biology environment. The spread of projects - from cell-free synthetic biology and aptamer design to cryogenic microscopy and neuromorphic nanopores - means the right fit depends less on your exact degree title and more on which lab's tools and questions you want to own for four years.

About EPFL

EPFL (Ecole Polytechnique Federale de Lausanne) is one of Europe's leading technical universities, sitting on the shores of Lake Geneva. Its doctoral programs are organised as EDBB-style schools that centralise admission, training and career development, and its graduates move easily into Swiss biotech, pharma and deep-tech employers.
